key_insight: UniT learns a unified "physical language"—a latent action tokenizer grounded by visual consequences—that aligns egocentric human data with humanoid actions, enabling scalable human-to-humanoid transfer despite kinematic mismatch.
problem_solved: Overcomes the scarcity of robot-collected data and the cross-embodiment / kinematic mismatch between humans and humanoids by grounding actions in shared visual outcomes rather than direct joint mappings.
method: Unified Latent Action Tokenizer: discretize actions into shared tokens representing actionable primitives across embodiments.
Visual Anchoring: use egocentric visual consequences as a common grounding to map human motion into tokens compatible with humanoid controllers.
Train policies and world models in the token space so humanoid policies can be learned or simulated from abundant human video data without extensive robot data.
impact: Enables scaling humanoid foundation models using massive egocentric human datasets, reducing robot data requirements and accelerating policy learning, transfer, and generalization for embodied AI.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: egocentric human video -> visual anchoring -> latent action tokens -> humanoid policy execution
Side-by-side comparison chart: data efficiency and transfer performance using UniT vs. conventional kinematic retargeting

paper_title: UniT: Toward a Unified Physical Language for Human-to-Humanoid Policy Learning and World Modeling
paper_authors: Boyu Chen, Yi Chen, Lu Qiu, Jerry Bai, Yuying Ge
